- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, creating a false peak followed by a sharp drop.
- Model underestimates prices during mean-reversion phases, particularly when prices are near historical lows or after a sharp decline.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, suggesting model struggles with short-term volatility or end-of-horizon adjustment.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — it takes 2–3 days to adjust downward, while true price often reverses faster.
- When price is rising steadily, model tends to overfit the trend and extrapolate too far, especially in the 15–25 day range.
- Model underestimates price volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <75), leading to overly smooth forecasts that miss sharp reversals.
- Model often fails to capture the “rebound” after a sharp drop — it underestimates the magnitude of the recovery, especially if the drop was driven by policy or supply shocks.
